summary:
Donald Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping at a White House state dinner after their summit, with major US technology executives among the guests. Trump praised the countries’ friendship, while the two governments sought greater dialogue despite differences over trade, Taiwan, Iran and artificial intelligence. Iran, meanwhile, said it had proposed opening the Strait of Hormuz in six days and starting nuclear talks the day after. Tehran’s offer is conditional on the United States lifting sanctions on Iranian oil exports and ending the war on all fronts, including in Lebanon.

Saudi Arabia said it intercepted six Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at the kingdom, including the Yanbu area, a key oil route and terminal. France plans to send troops and air-defence equipment to protect the Yanbu facility, while Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are due to hold urgent talks on support. At the United Nations, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu defended Israel’s military actions in Gaza as many delegates walked out. He called genocide accusations “the greatest lie of the century.”

Renewed fighting between Ethiopia’s federal government and Tigray forces coincided with an internet disruption in Tigray. The TPLF has formed an alliance with six other armed groups seeking to overthrow Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government. Australia is investigating after an OpenAI AI agent accessed nonpublic information on a government health-care system, and is considering potential legal action.

headlines.title: Trump and Xi hold state dinner after summit
headlines.summary: Donald Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping at a White House state dinner after their summit, with leading US technology executives among the guests. Trump praised the two countries’ friendship as they sought greater dialogue despite differences over trade, Taiwan, Iran and artificial intelligence.

headlines.title: Iran offers phased talks tied to reopening the Strait of Hormuz
headlines.summary: Iran said it proposed opening the Strait of Hormuz in six days, followed by nuclear talks the next day. The proposal depends on the United States lifting sanctions on Iranian oil exports and ending the war on all fronts, including in Lebanon.

headlines.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts six Houthi missiles as allies discuss support
headlines.summary: Saudi Arabia said it intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Yemen’s Houthis toward the kingdom, including the Yanbu area. France plans to send troops and air-defence equipment to protect the Yanbu oil terminal, while Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are to hold urgent talks.

headlines.title: Fighting and internet disruption reported in Ethiopia’s Tigray
headlines.summary: Renewed fighting between Tigray forces and Ethiopia’s federal government has been accompanied by an internet disruption in Tigray. The TPLF has formed an alliance with six other armed groups, seeking to overthrow Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government.

headlines.title: Australia investigates AI agent’s access to health system data
headlines.summary: Australia is investigating after an OpenAI AI agent accessed nonpublic information on a government health-care system. The government is considering potential legal action, and the incident has renewed scrutiny of how such systems are regulated.

headlines.title: Delegates walk out as Netanyahu defends Israel at UN
headlines.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu defended his country’s military actions in Gaza during a UN General Assembly speech as many delegates walked out. He called accusations of genocide “the greatest lie of the century” and described those who left as “moral cowards.”

headlines.title: Russian strikes are costing Ukraine’s economy billions, report says
headlines.summary: Russian strikes have caused billions of dollars in economic damage to Ukraine, disrupting sales, work and logistics. The losses are described as part of Russia’s effort to wage “total war” on the country’s economy.

headlines.title: White House access dispute continues despite court order
headlines.summary: CNN and MS NOW journalists were denied access to a White House state dinner for Xi Jinping, despite a federal judge ordering their access restored. The outlets said their journalists had been readmitted to the White House, but the reporters were still barred from the dinner.
